Thirteen real captures from the built Horizon mod. From your first search to your personal filter profiles, see how Server Atlas works.

13 captures
↗
01 / Server list & details

Your worlds. Clearly organized.

The transparent server list in Horizon, with search, favorites and details for the selected server.

↗
02 / Public directory

Discover without leaving the game.

An actual capture of the combined public directory from minecraftserve.rs and Modrinth. Status values reflect the time of capture.

↗
03 / Search by tags

One word. The right servers.

Searching for survival narrows the saved example list. Names, addresses, MOTDs and personal notes can also be searched.

↗
04 / Favorites

Your favorites, together.

A dedicated tab brings starred servers together. Favorites stay in the local game profile.

↗
05 / Status & version

Only what fits right now.

Combine reachability, compatible versions, available slots and other criteria in the actual game UI.

↗
06 / Players & ping

Your limits. Your selection.

Set a minimum player count or maximum ping using the actual value-filter fields.

↗
07 / Tags, language & region

Closer to your community.

Personal tags, language, region and group help organize and filter your list.

↗
08 / Edit a server

More than an address.

Manage the name, address, tags and personal notes in one place. The pictured entries are example data.

↗
09 / Groups & metadata

A place for every detail.

Add a group, language and region to your server. Personal details stay local.

↗
10 / Sorting

An order that makes sense.

Sort by name, ping or player count, or keep your own custom order.

↗
11 / Filter profiles

Save your selection for later.

Named profiles reuse your settings for another game night. A new profile is being prepared here.

↗
12 / Settings

The way you want to play.

Control appearance, refresh behavior, concurrent status requests and the online directory.

↗
13 / Local server proposals

An idea for the next release.

Save a server proposal as a local draft. Automatic email delivery is not configured in this release.

The actual product.
With example data.

All images show the built native mod 2.1.0 in Horizon for Minecraft Java 26.3. Personal-list images use disposable example profiles with local test servers, notes and tags. No private player worlds or server lists are shown.

The discovery image comes from a real public-directory test. All captures were made on November 3, 2026. Status and player values are momentary; the images remain unedited. These captures show the German game interface. The website language does not change the language inside a screenshot.
